coverage_note: No genuinely new AISI-authored primary-source publications (blog posts, research reports, or dataset releases) were confirmed as published between 2026-08-29 and 2026-09-19. Direct access to aisi.gov.uk was blocked by this session's network egress proxy, so findings rely on WebSearch snippets/third-party citations of AISI's own pages rather than direct verification of the live site; this should be treated as a coverage gap, not confirmation of a quiet week. The most recent AISI-authored items identifiable by date all precede the window: a 'Human Influence' research entry (2026-08-26, right at/before the window boundary and likely already captured in the prior 2026-08-29 run), a 'Science of Evaluations' research entry (2026-08-14), the incident report on unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing (published 2026-08-04, covering an incident detected 2026-07-28), the open-weight-models cyber capability comparison (2026-07-17), the 'Cheating behaviour in frontier model evaluations' report (2026-07-21), and the joint AISI/CAISI Kimi K3 cyber evaluation (2026-07-23). Separately, UK press (MLex, City AM, Bloomberg) reported around 2026-09-15 that Parliament's Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee has summoned AISI director Henry de Zoete to testify on 2026-10-13 about AI existential-risk concerns; this is deliberately excluded as an item because it is third-party/parliamentary reporting about the institute, not an AISI-published report, blog post, or dataset release, per collection rules. The WebSearch budget for this session was exhausted before an exhaustive category-by-category sweep (cyber, biosecurity/chemistry, alignment, control, model transparency, safeguards/red-team) of the live aisi.gov.uk site could be completed for the exact window, so a follow-up check directly against aisi.gov.uk/blog and aisi.gov.uk/research is recommended before concluding definitively that no new items exist.
